summary.title: Lessons from Keith Rabois Essay 3: How to be an Effective Executive
summary.one_liner: You learn how to act as a proactive leader rather than a reactive manager by focusing on team inputs, high-leverage work, calendar design, information gathering, simple metrics, decision-making rules, and matching autonomy to task maturity.
keywords: how to delegate to junior staff
takeaways: Think of yourself as a leader driving output rather than a manager reacting to situations, and judge yourself by output per team member.
Focus on team inputs and clear, simple objectives with paired indicators, rather than only outcome targets.
Proactively design your calendar around your top 3 weekly priorities, audit it regularly, and batch similar tasks.
Gather raw information through skip-levels, wandering the office, and written reports, and decide by knowledge rather than position.
Match management style and delegation to the employee's task maturity, and extend rope on low-consequence decisions.
summary.summary:
This essay, the third in a series by Keith Rabois' portfolio-company talks as relayed by the author (delian.io), sets out a framework for effective executives. It covers leading versus managing, measuring output relative to team size, focusing on inputs, and spending time on high-leverage activities such as all-hands presentations, dashboards, and targeted feedback. It also gives practical guidance on calendar audits, meeting types (1:1s, staff meetings, decision meetings, operational reviews), and deciding by knowledge rather than position. The final section offers a motivation-versus-capability framework and a conviction-versus-consequence grid for delegation. The piece draws on examples and ideas from Andy Grove, Jeff Bezos, Paul Graham, Claire Hughes Johnson, and others.</summary>
